concept: Recursive queries with SEARCH and CYCLE
current_formulation: PostgreSQL 18 supports WITH RECURSIVE with the SEARCH and CYCLE clauses as a rewrite into the hand-written form, and the cycle mark values are optional (feature T133).

steps.formulation: SQL:1999 defines WITH RECURSIVE and the SEARCH and CYCLE clauses, with mandatory cycle mark values.
steps.quote: CYCLE <cycle column list> SET <cycle mark column> TO <cycle mark value> DEFAULT <non-cycle mark value> USING <path column>

steps.formulation: PostgreSQL 8.4 implements WITH RECURSIVE without SEARCH and CYCLE, and the manual tells users to detect cycles by hand with an array of visited values.
steps.quote: The standard method for handling such situations is to compute an array of the already-visited values.

criticism.quote: The original discussion about recursive CTEs briefly mentioned these as something to do later but then it was never mentioned again.

steps.formulation: PostgreSQL adds SEARCH and CYCLE as a rewrite into the hand-written form (commit of 2021-02-01, released in 14 on 2021-09-30).
steps.quote: These clauses can be rewritten into queries using existing syntax, and that is what this patch does in the rewriter.

steps.formulation: Following a draft of a later standard, the cycle mark values become optional and default to TRUE and FALSE.
steps.quote: Per SQL:202x draft, in the CYCLE clause of a recursive query, the cycle mark values can be of type boolean and can be omitted
